rounds.text: Manilam Industries faces a significant disconnect between its premium valuation and its deteriorating operational performance. The business is currently burning cash, evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -6 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -7 Cr in March 2026 [E27, E28]. This cash crunch is exacerbated by a concerning increase in working capital days from 73.5 to 134 days and high debtor days of 223 [E46, E47]. Furthermore, the stock is priced for aggressive growth that the underlying financials do not support, as the reverse DCF implies an 18.8% earnings growth rate [E39] while the company struggles with low returns on equity of 3.9% [E13]. Conceded: the company has reduced its borrowings from Rs 62 Cr to Rs 51 Cr [E31] and maintains a price-to-book ratio of 1.65x, which is lower than the sector benchmark of 1.91x [E7].
